cases.note: "a " has no delimiter, so it is a tombstone; its key strips to a, which it deletes.
"a<TAB> " has a delimiter, so it sets a; the cell strips to empty.
A row whose key is empty has no effect.
An empty line is an empty-key row: ignored, not a tombstone.
With stripping on, a key of spaces resolves to empty and the row is ignored, with or without a delimiter.
With stripping off, a key of one space is a real key.
Trailing spaces are stripped from the raw field, then tokens are decoded, so an encoded newline survives.
A later record changes a key's value, not its order.
A key written <#>foo reads as #foo and is data, not a comment.
<#>_defaults_# is a data key named #_defaults_#, not a marker.
Markers, comments, an empty-key row, a CRLF row, encoded fields, a tombstone and another algorithm's marker all feed the crc32 segment as raw bytes; the checksum lines themselves are not data.
